report_name: Helix Ransomware Group Claims Attack on American Campus

threat_actors.name: Helix
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that has claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on American Campus. The group employs double extortion tactics, exfiltrating data and threatening to publish it if the ransom is not paid.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion of victims through data encryption and the threat of data leakage.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Helix ransomware payload was allegedly deployed to encrypt systems across the American Campus network, rendering them unusable as part of a double extortion scheme.

attack_patterns.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
attack_patterns.description: The Helix group claimed to have exfiltrated sensitive data from American Campus to their own cloud storage before deploying ransomware, a core component of their double extortion strategy.

malware.name: Helix Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the Helix group to encrypt victim systems. In the attack against American Campus, it was used to encrypt files as part of a double extortion attack.

identities.name: American Campus
identities.description: A major US-based student housing provider with an estimated annual revenue of $1 billion, targeted by the Helix ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: GoFile Data Leak Host
infrastructure.description: The file-sharing service GoFile was named by the Helix group as the platform where they would release links to the data exfiltrated from American Campus.
